metadata.title: Noemorph consciousness and mind research corpus
metadata.methodology: A citation-first, open-world collection organized from Robert Lawrence Kuhn's inclusive 2024 landscape, the 474-entry Closer To Truth Landscape index, systematic and scoping reviews, primary works, and authoritative scholarly references. Dated research supplements extend independently audited strata while retaining theory boundaries, source roles, evidence profiles, open questions, and collection provenance. Discovery-frame candidates remain separate from reviewed catalog records, and conceptual synthesis remains deferred.
metadata.coverage_notice: There is no defensible fixed denominator for ‘all theories.’ Noemorph reports protocol coverage, unresolved strata, and discovery yield rather than declaring the catalog complete.

discovery_frames.name: TSC 2024 research-topic taxonomy
discovery_frames.type: Scope-control taxonomy; topics are not counted as theories

gate_requirements: Every published catalog record has at least two retained citation locators and exact destinations.
Scientific theories, philosophical positions, frameworks, traditions, and social-cognition theories remain separately typed.
Citation title, author, work identity, and DOI destination pass independent semantic review.
At least 95% of registered discovery-frame items are screened overall and 85% in every mandatory stratum.
At least 90% of records are anchored to a primary or authoritative self-exposition source, or reviewed waiver.
Unresolved identity and duplicate candidates fall below the protocol threshold.
Two independent reviewers approve the coverage report before synthesis begins.

collections.title: Noemorph neuroscience and clinical-state gap packet
collections.purpose: Provisional, citation-first additions that fill distinct neuroscience, computational, temporal, anesthesia, sleep, and disorders-of-consciousness gaps in the base catalog.
collections.selection_policy: Each candidate is absent from the base catalog as a named record, has a defensible identity distinct from adjacent entries, and retains at least two exact peer-reviewed DOI locators. Foundational theories, clinical-state mechanisms, and measurement frameworks remain separately typed.
collections.source_policy: Defining self-expositions and primary empirical papers are preferred. Reviews are used to bound evidence and disagreement, never to convert framework-level support into validation of a constitutive theory.
collections.deduplication_note: Beautiful Loop Theory is separated from generic Free-Energy Principle and predictive-processing entries; criticality from the Entropic Brain Hypothesis; Neural Hierarchy from GNWT, RPT, DIT, and Apical Amplification; PCI from IIT and generic disorders-of-consciousness records; Cognitive Unbinding, Neural Inertia, and cortical bistability from the umbrella anesthesia/state records.
collections.synthesis_policy: These records remain provisional collection objects. Cross-theory synthesis, endorsement, ranking, and causal unification are out of scope until coverage and independent review gates are met.

collections.title: Awareness, selfhood, metacognition, social cognition, comparative cognition, and machine-mind gap audit
collections.scope: Provisional records absent from the 2026-08-29 Noemorph base catalog. The collection prioritizes awareness, metacognition, selfhood, developmental and comparative social cognition, and machine theory-of-mind. One adjacent attention theory is retained with an explicit boundary note.
collections.method: Exact-name and keyword audit of the base catalog followed by source verification against DOI publisher records, official proceedings, and peer-reviewed primary or authoritative review literature.
collections.attribution_policy: Each record preserves its own proponents, claim scope, evidence profile, and citations. No inter-theory relationship, convergence, or synthesis claim is asserted.

collections.title: Noemorph philosophy, arguments, and historical traditions gap additions
collections.method: Exact-name and semantic gap audit against the 207-record base catalog, followed by source-level checking against primary works, primary-source translations, DOI records, and authoritative scholarly reference entries.
collections.source_policy: Each candidate retains at least two exact HTTPS locators. Summaries report source-attributable claims only; boundary notes identify common overextensions and translation risks.
collections.coverage_note: These are independent, provisional catalog candidates. The collection does not claim exhaustiveness and asserts no cross-record relationships, equivalences, or synthesis. Living and internally diverse traditions are represented through named texts and interpreters rather than as uniform civilizational views.

collections.name: Kuhn sections 17–18: anomalous proposals and explanatory challenges
collections.method: Manual identity and boundary selection from the reproducible Closer To Truth discovery registry; source descriptions were paraphrased and all entries retain exact frame locators.
collections.phase_policy: Collection only; no conceptual relationship edges or synthesis claims.

collections.title: Noemorph neuroscience and mind-science breadth packet
collections.purpose: Provisional, citation-first breadth additions spanning neglected neural and biophysical proposals, bounded clinical-state models, comparative consciousness, artificial-consciousness assessment and architectures, and foundational perception, memory, emotion, embodiment, and agency models relevant to a systematic map of mind.
collections.selection_policy: Every record is name- and alias-checked against all catalog shards present at final validation on 2026-08-30, retains at least two exact HTTPS scholarly locators, and is included only when its identity and claim boundary can be stated without inferring inter-theory relations.
collections.source_policy: Defining expositions and primary empirical papers are preferred. Reviews and replications are labelled by authority role and are used to assess scope or evidence, not to manufacture consensus.
collections.deduplication_note: Broad cognitive mechanisms are cataloged only as bounded models, not as theories of phenomenal consciousness. Existing entries for global workspace, recurrent processing, integrated information, predictive processing, electromagnetic-field theories, anesthesia, epilepsy, dreaming/protoconsciousness, body ownership, agency, and affective consciousness were treated as collision risks rather than umbrella permission.
collections.synthesis_policy: No cross-theory relation, ranking, endorsement, or synthesis is asserted in this packet. All records remain provisional collection objects pending domain review.

collections.title: Cognitive breadth expansion: attention, self, agency, time, memory, language, affect, development, comparative, collective, and machine social cognition
collections.scope: Provisional breadth records absent from the merged 249-record Noemorph corpus. This shard covers named theories, models, frameworks, and bounded empirical constructs across cognitive domains adjacent to or constitutive of research on mind and consciousness.
collections.method: Exact-name, alias, and citation-locator collision audit against catalog.json and every 2026-08-30 shard, followed by verification against DOI metadata, official proceedings, publisher records, PubMed, and the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
collections.boundary_policy: Adjacent attention, timing, memory, group, and machine models explicitly state what they do and do not claim about phenomenal consciousness.
collections.attribution_policy: Claims remain local to each named record and cited authors. No inter-theory relationship, convergence, compatibility, causal synthesis, or ranking is asserted.

collections.title: Noemorph philosophy-of-mind and global historical breadth additions
collections.method: Normalized exact-name and alias audit against the 249-record merged corpus, followed by record-level source checking against primary works, DOI-indexed scholarship, institutional editions, and specialist reference entries.
collections.source_policy: Every record retains at least two exact HTTPS locators and distinguishes original texts, translations, author-maintained copies, institutional editions, and authoritative secondary scholarship. No relationship edges or cross-tradition equivalences are asserted.
collections.coverage_note: This provisional shard broadens analytic philosophy, perception, self, agency, personal identity, phenomenology, ancient and early-modern psychology, and named Islamic, Jewish, Indian, East Asian, African, Maori, and Northern Ojibwe articulations. It is not exhaustive and does not treat any tradition as internally uniform.
exclusions: Homuncular functionalism was excluded as a version of the existing Functionalism record pending a version-level ontology.

Contingent representationalism and transparency theory were excluded because the current corpus already contains First-Order Representationalism and self-representational positions; a versioning policy is needed before splitting them.
Sensorimotor and enacted-perception candidates were excluded as duplicates of Sensorimotor Contingency Theory and Enactivism.
Radical neurophenomenology was excluded as a version of the existing Neurophenomenology record.

Named dual-aspect variants, Swinburne substance dualism, emergent dualism, neo-Thomist dualism, and Tye representationalism were excluded because the present ontology already contains their parent positions and does not yet support version records consistently.
Altered-state, anomalous-experience, and clinical challenge records were left to the separately scoped state-and-challenge audit.

collections.title: States, clinical assessment, and consciousness-measurement breadth packet
collections.scope: Distinct attributable state constructs, assessment instruments, experimental paradigms, psychometric frameworks, and expert evidential positions spanning disorders of consciousness, anesthesia, sleep and dreaming, psychedelic and contemplative states, interoception and metacognition, development, comparative consciousness, and neural measurement.
collections.method: Human-curated candidate selection followed by exact name and alias collision checks against every extant catalog shard, DOI resolution against Crossref, and source-level boundary review.
collections.boundary_policy: Every record states whether it is a state construct, assessment instrument, experimental paradigm, signal statistic, or evidential declaration; none is silently promoted to a causal or constitutive theory of consciousness.
collections.citation_policy: Each record retains at least two exact HTTPS primary, validation, systematic-review, guideline, or official locators. DOI metadata are resolved at build time; official declarations are manually verified.
collections.attribution_policy: Claims remain local to named authors, instruments, paradigms, and documents. No inferred compatibility, causal relationship, ranking, or synthesis is asserted.
collections.deduplication_policy: Names and aliases are normalized and compared with catalog.json and every catalog supplement present at build time; conceptual neighbors are retained only when their target and method are independently bounded.

collections.title: Noemorph cross-cultural, historical, religious-philosophical, and Indigenous breadth additions
collections.method: Candidate construction from record-specific primary translations, peer-reviewed scholarship, institutional editions, community-authored frameworks, specialist encyclopedias, and exact-name/alias collision auditing against the registered Noemorph corpus.
collections.source_policy: Every record retains at least two HTTPS locators. DOI resolution and locator availability are recorded separately from interpretive review. Community-authored sources are preferred for living Indigenous frameworks; externally theorized ethnographic models are labeled as such.
collections.coverage_note: This provisional shard separates named traditions and thinkers instead of treating geographic regions as single theories. It includes South Asian, Buddhist, Sikh, Jaina, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Arabic-Islamic, Jewish, African, Indigenous American, Pacific, and ancient religious-philosophical records. It is not exhaustive.
collections.translation_policy: Key non-English terms remain visible. English glosses are treated as provisional, polysemy and textual layers are noted per record, and no cross-tradition equivalence edges are asserted.
collections.community_and_ethnography_policy: Living Indigenous frameworks are bounded to named authors, communities, institutions, or public scholarship. External anthropological syntheses remain attributed to their theorists and are not presented as uniform community belief.
exclusions: Parent theories already represented in the merged corpus—including Advaita, Sāṃkhya–Yoga, Yogācāra, Madhyamaka, Dzogchen, Mahāmudrā, Pratyabhijñā, Tiantai, Huayan in Fazang, Wang Yangming, Akan, Yorùbá, and existing Māori/Ojibwe records—were not renamed and double-counted.
Generic pan-Indigenous medicine-wheel, animism, shamanism, chakra, and 'Eastern mind' headings were excluded because they collapse distinct communities or lack bounded attribution.
Restricted, initiatory, or community-controlled knowledge was not sought; only publicly available scholarship and institutional records were used.
Cross-cultural synthesis, equivalence claims, and graph relationships remain deferred until candidate review and identity resolution are complete.

collections.title: Noemorph emerging scientific and formal consciousness breadth packet
collections.base_catalog: data/catalog.json plus registered catalog supplements present on 2026-08-30
collections.purpose: Provisional, citation-first additions for recent and underrepresented scientific, computational, formal, methodological, and artificial-consciousness proposals that were absent from the merged Noemorph corpus.
collections.selection_policy: Each record is an attributable named proposal or bounded framework, is checked against names and aliases in the merged catalog, retains at least two exact HTTPS scholarly locators, and states what its sources do not establish.
collections.source_policy: Defining primary papers and publisher DOI records are preferred. Independent reviews, comparisons, or empirical developments are labeled by role. Two arXiv sources are retained only for the explicitly preprint-stage Digital Consciousness Model and its comparison framework.
collections.deduplication_note: Existing entries for free-energy/active inference, predictive processing, criticality, integrated information, global workspace, recurrent processing, functionalism, and AI theory-derived indicators were treated as collision constraints. Near-neighbor additions are bounded to a later named proposal, formal extension, or distinct methodological claim.
collections.temporal_note: Snapshot as of 2026-08-30. Publication year follows the earliest dated Crossref publication event; online-first papers may precede their issue year.
collections.synthesis_policy: No cross-theory relation, ranking, endorsement, or synthetic conclusion is asserted. All records remain provisional collection objects pending domain and citation review.

collections.title: Noemorph contemporary consciousness continuation supplement
collections.purpose: A conservative continuation packet of source-bounded clinical, dream-research, and artificial-consciousness methods that passed a two-source promotion gate.
collections.selection_policy: Each row is absent from the checked catalog as an exact name or alias, has a stable named identity distinct from adjacent records, uses a catalog-allowlisted kind, and retains at least two distinct authoritative or primary locators. COGITATE is excluded because its results belong as evidence additions to existing IIT and GNWT profiles.
collections.source_policy: Defining peer-reviewed studies, independent or cross-cultural validations, official versioned program materials, and primary scholarly elaborations are retained with exact locators. Two sources establish traceability, not truth or evidential independence; dependence is stated in each evidence profile.
collections.deduplication_note: DoC Common Data Elements is infrastructure rather than a diagnostic measure; SECONDs remains separate from CRS-R and other abbreviated DoC tools; LuCiD is a retrospective dream scale rather than physiological lucid-dream verification; Targeted Dream Incubation is a specific N1 protocol rather than broad Dream Engineering; ACT is a training-restricted language proposal distinct from ConsScale, theory-derived AI indicators, naturalness-constrained tests, and bilateral simulation tests.
collections.synthesis_policy: These are provisional collection objects. The supplement does not endorse a measure, infer phenomenality, rank theories, or license semantic synthesis before specialist review and broader coverage checks.

collections.title: Noemorph cross-cultural continuation: bounded accounts of social selfhood, relational personhood, and neurodiversity
collections.method: Eight records were promoted from a 26-item acquisition review after exact-name and scope comparison against the complete 577-record catalog. Promotion required two distinct exact primary, authoritative, or scholarly HTTPS locators, an allowlisted catalog kind, explicit differentiation from neighboring records, and no unresolved source-metadata, translation, lineage, or community-governance blocker.
collections.source_policy: Each record retains exactly the two locators that cleared promotion review. DOI-bearing works include the DOI when known; locator availability and interpretive review remain separately described.
collections.coverage_note: This continuation adds bounded modern African, Dalit, anthropological, feminist-phenomenological, Latina feminist, autistic-led, and neurodiversity records. It does not claim regional completeness and does not treat every entry as a theory of phenomenal consciousness.
collections.translation_policy: Source-language and community terms remain attributed to named authors and settings. A shared English gloss is never treated as proof of cross-tradition identity.
collections.non_equivalence_policy: No conceptual-equivalence, historical-lineage, or causal relationship edge follows from co-occurrence, topic similarity, or semantic proximity. Anthropologists' analytical models remain distinct from community self-descriptions, and social or normative accounts remain distinct from mechanistic consciousness theories.
collections.promotion_gate: Source-screened and schema-ready, but still provisional. Passage-level claims, critical reception, and normal human catalog review remain required before any later synthesis phase.

collections.title: Noemorph frontier science continuation supplement
collections.base_catalog: data/catalog.json plus registered supplements present on 2026-08-30
collections.purpose: Citation-first additions for five recent, named scientific or computational consciousness proposals absent from the merged Noemorph catalog.
collections.selection_policy: Each record is an attributable proposal with a bounded identity, a complete research profile, and at least two distinct authoritative scholarly works. Promotion records descriptive inclusion, not acceptance or evidential success.
collections.source_policy: Defining peer-reviewed DOI works are paired with distinct theoretical precursors, methodological treatments, critical analysis, or empirical sources for the explanandum. Shared authorship and intellectual lineage are disclosed, and no contextual citation is treated as independent theory-specific confirmation.
collections.deduplication_policy: Identity review preserved explicit separations from Joint Determinant Theory, generic higher-order and Radical Plasticity families, attention-selection theories, Beautiful Loop Theory, general Algorithmic Information Theory, the Minimal Phenomenal Experience and ARAS record, the Pure-Awareness Entropy Model, and the Entropic Brain Hypothesis.
collections.temporal_note: Snapshot as of 2026-08-30. Newly published and preprint-stage critical work remains subject to metadata, replication, and identity review.
collections.synthesis_policy: These are provisional collection objects. The supplement asserts no cross-theory connection, ranking, endorsement, or novel synthesis, and all five records retain explicit non-establishment and open-question fields.

profile_collections.name: Core consciousness-theory research-profile enrichments
profile_collections.purpose: Deepen high-centrality foundational records whose original entries had citations and summaries but lacked explicit claim boundaries, evidence limitations, and open research questions needed for defensible semantic comparison.
profile_collections.selection_policy: This first tranche prioritizes major scientific theory families and shared explananda that recur throughout consciousness research. It does not rank or endorse them.
profile_collections.identity_policy: Enrichments may not change record identity, name, kind, domain, tradition, proponents, status, summary, or original citations. New evidence may only be appended with an exact locator.
profile_collections.synthesis_policy: No relation among records is asserted. Profiles remain provisional collection objects pending specialist review.

profile_collections.name: Core consciousness-theory research-profile enrichments, tranche 2
profile_collections.purpose: Deepen a second set of foundational but shallow records with explicit claim boundaries, evidence limits, and open questions suitable for cautious semantic comparison.
profile_collections.selection_policy: This tranche covers cellular, computational, higher-order, self-model, metacognitive, and phenomenal-construct records that recur in the catalog but lacked full research profiles. It does not rank or endorse them.
profile_collections.identity_policy: Enrichments preserve record identity and original citations. Where a retained locator is incomplete or mismatched, the profile records that limitation rather than silently repairing or relying on it.
profile_collections.synthesis_policy: Conceptual exposition, component-level plausibility, and independent discriminating evidence are separated. No relation among records is asserted, and every profile remains provisional pending specialist review.

limitations: Report, attention, task relevance, and confidence can contribute to canonical late signatures.
The 2025 adversarial collaboration found results compatible with some predictions while challenging offset ignition and parts of the proposed prefrontal representation profile.
evidence_profile.independence: The appended Cogitate Consortium study was designed by proponents and theory-neutral researchers and preregistered divergent predictions; it does not deliver a binary verdict on GNWT.

open_questions: Which ignition signatures survive no-report and task-irrelevant designs?

claim_scope.target: How some contents become conscious by exerting sufficiently broad and durable influence across distributed processes.
claim_scope.level: Functional cognitive architecture and philosophical interpretation of distributed neural processing.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A quantitative fame threshold, that all globally influential information is phenomenal, or that a central workspace or observer exists.

basis: Dennett's retained 2001 paper is the primary statement of the cerebral-fame formulation and its explanatory aims.

limitations: The formulation is not operationalized by a unique quantitative measure, so ordinary access, memory, report, and executive influence can be mistaken for the target property.

evidence_profile.independence: The retained primary source is theoretical exposition; the encyclopedia is an independent overview, not a discriminating experimental test.

open_questions: How can cerebral fame be measured without reducing it to reportability or workspace access?
Which prediction distinguishes this formulation from Multiple Drafts and global-workspace architectures?

records.boundary_note: Information closure is not ordinary causal isolation, thermodynamic closure, mutual information, or IIT's integrated information. Claims about level and content depend on selecting system boundaries, environmental variables, temporal scales, and coarse-grainings.

claim_scope.target: Whether non-trivially closed informational processes can identify conscious systems and characterize their level or content.
claim_scope.level: Information theory, dynamical processes, system-environment relations, and computational modeling.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That closure is sufficient for phenomenality, that one privileged coarse-graining is available from data, or that formal examples validate the measure in brains.

basis: The retained 2020 primary paper defines the proposal and develops its formal motivation.
The retained 2021 classification paper independently analyzes ICT's explanatory profile relative to other consciousness models.
limitations: Formal coherence and model examples do not show that estimated closure tracks consciousness rather than autonomy, predictability, or model choice.
Empirical estimation is sensitive to unobserved variables, finite data, boundary selection, temporal resolution, and coarse-graining.
evidence_profile.independence: The independent retained source is a systematic classification, not a direct empirical validation. No retained adversarial or preregistered test establishes ICT-specific predictions.

open_questions: How can the relevant system boundary and coarse-graining be selected without using consciousness labels circularly?
Which feasible observation distinguishes ICT from integrated-information, predictive, or generic autonomy measures?

records.boundary_note: HOSS models higher-order inference and awareness report, which may concern metacognitive access rather than phenomenal character. It should not be generalized to all predictive processing or treated as empirical support for every higher-order theory.

claim_scope.target: How a higher-order generative model can infer whether first-order perceptual content is present and thereby structure awareness reports.
claim_scope.level: Bayesian computation, perceptual decision, metacognition, and report.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That Bayesian inference is sufficient for experience, that report and phenomenality are identical, or that the modeled state space has a unique neural implementation.

basis: The retained peer-reviewed paper provides an explicit computational formulation and relates it to perceptual and metacognitive phenomena.
The retained preprint supplies provenance for the same model's development.
limitations: Agreement with report behavior can support a decision or metacognitive model without establishing a constitutive theory of consciousness.
Model flexibility and unobserved higher-order states complicate parameter identification and comparison with first-order Bayesian alternatives.
evidence_profile.independence: The two retained locators are publication stages of one proponent-authored work. They do not constitute independent empirical validation or replication.

open_questions: Which preregistered behavioral or neural prediction uniquely favors HOSS over first-order signal-detection or metacognitive models?
Can latent higher-order state-space parameters be recovered reliably across tasks and observers?
How does HOSS address no-report consciousness and nonperceptual experience?

basis: First-person reports and philosophical analysis motivate distinguishing experience from availability and performance.

records.name: Beautiful Loop Theory
records.status: newly proposed · formalized · not independently validated
records.status_note: The 2025 paper is the defining peer-reviewed exposition. The 2026 active-inference review establishes the surrounding research program, but it is not an independent test of Beautiful Loop Theory.
records.summary: Beautiful Loop Theory proposes three conditions for consciousness: an epistemic field or unified world model, inferential competition that binds uncertainty-reducing hypotheses into that model, and epistemic depth produced by recurrent sharing of Bayesian beliefs through a hierarchy. It formalizes the third condition with a precision-controlling hyper-model whose states govern weighting across levels of inference.
records.scope: Computational and putatively constitutive account of conscious state and content within active inference; extended by its authors to sleep, dreaming, meditation, psychedelics, and artificial agents.
records.boundary_note: Catalog separately from the Free-Energy Principle, Active Inference, and generic predictive-processing approaches because BLT adds named necessary conditions and a precision hyper-model. Its suggested neuromodulatory and electromagnetic broadcast routes are implementation proposals, not established consequences of active inference.

claim_scope.target: Minimal conditions proposed for conscious experience and its integration across states.
claim_scope.level: Computational / functional, with candidate neural implementations.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That active inference alone is sufficient for consciousness, that the three conditions are empirically necessary, or that any proposed biological broadcast channel is uniquely correct.

basis: A peer-reviewed defining theory paper with an explicit three-condition architecture and formal precision-control proposal.
A broader peer-reviewed 2026 review identifies shared, potentially testable consciousness commitments across active-inference models.
limitations: No published theory-specific experimental program yet discriminates BLT from GNWT, recurrent processing, higher-order, or other active-inference accounts.
Many applications to altered states are explanatory fits rather than risky prospective tests.
evidence_profile.independence: The second source overlaps intellectually and by one author with the defining paper; independent corroboration remains absent.

open_questions: Which operational measures separately identify epistemic field, Bayesian binding, and epistemic depth in vivo?
What observation would distinguish the precision hyper-model from ordinary hierarchical predictive control?
Which organisms or artificial systems satisfy the conditions without importing behavioral report as the criterion?

records.name: ALARM theory of consciousness
records.status: newly proposed · evolving formulation · not independently validated
records.status_note: The 2023 exposition presented a two-level theory; the 2025 expansion explicitly distinguishes three phenomena and functions. Version and date must be retained when comparing claims.
records.summary: ALARM distinguishes basic arousal, general alertness, and reflexive self-consciousness rather than treating phenomenal consciousness as one undifferentiated capacity. It assigns basic arousal an alarm-and-survival role through intervention in slow homeostatic updating, general alertness roles in advanced learning and decision-making, and reflexive self-consciousness a role in future-directed planning that models self and other agents.
records.scope: Evolutionary and functional partition of phenomenal consciousness, intended to constrain searches for distinct neural correlates at subcortical and cortical levels.
records.boundary_note: Do not merge with affective/brainstem consciousness theories or multidimensional state frameworks. ALARM is a named evolutionary-functional partition that assigns different roles to three consciousness phenomena; it does not merely assert that arousal is multidimensional.

claim_scope.target: Functions and evolutionary organization of three forms of phenomenal consciousness.
claim_scope.level: Functional / evolutionary, with constraints on candidate neural correlates.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A complete constitutive mechanism, a unique anatomical substrate for each form, or that all conscious contents require reflexive self-consciousness.

basis: Two peer-reviewed self-expositions develop the framework from a two-level formulation into an explicit three-phenomenon account.
The account is constrained by comparative, arousal, homeostatic, learning, and self-modeling literatures reviewed by the authors.
limitations: The proposed functions are theoretical assignments rather than results of direct comparative or lesion-based adjudication.
Boundaries among arousal, alertness, attention, access, and phenomenal consciousness remain operationally difficult.
evidence_profile.independence: Both retained sources are by the theory's proponents; independent tests and critical comparisons are needed.

open_questions: Can basic arousal be dissociated from phenomenal consciousness without defining either through responsiveness?
Which phylogenetic and developmental transitions mark general alertness and reflexive self-consciousness?
Do the three proposed functions map to separable and necessary neural mechanisms?

records.name: Algorithmic Information Theory of Consciousness
records.status: formal proposal · limited direct testing
records.status_note: The framework supplies mathematical concepts and candidate complexity measures, but Kolmogorov complexity is not directly computable and available proxies are not specific to KT.
records.summary: The theory begins from the existence of consciousness and addresses structured experience by proposing that recurrent cognitive systems construct succinct generative models of their input-output streams. Compressive models organize phenomenal structure, while self-awareness is proposed to arise when a bidirectionally interacting system includes itself in a better model. Algorithmic complexity and mutual algorithmic information motivate candidate measurements of brain state and brain-world coupling.
records.scope: Formal account of structured experience and candidate state measures grounded in Kolmogorov complexity, model compression, and recurrent cognition.
records.boundary_note: Keep separate from IIT, Information Closure Theory, raw entropy accounts, and generic predictive processing. KT concerns compressive generative models and algorithmic regularity; it does not identify consciousness with maximal randomness or with a single Lempel-Ziv score.

claim_scope.target: The structure of conscious experience and computational preconditions for self-modeling.
claim_scope.level: Algorithmic / computational, with proposed neurophysiological measurement strategies.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That approximate compression metrics uniquely measure consciousness, that all model-building systems are conscious, or that algorithmic complexity solves the phenomenality question.

basis: A peer-reviewed formal exposition connects model compression, recurrent systems, and structured experience and lists candidate empirical probes.
A subsequent peer-reviewed information-generation theory explicitly compares KT with other information-centric accounts.
limitations: Kolmogorov complexity is uncomputable in the general case, so empirical studies rely on estimator- and data-dependent proxies.
Neural complexity changes occur across many states and theories and therefore do not by themselves discriminate KT.
evidence_profile.independence: The comparison source is independent of Ruffini but is theoretical rather than a targeted empirical test.

open_questions: Which feasible estimator best preserves the theory's distinction between structured complexity and noise?
What compression-based prediction differs from IIT, predictive processing, and generic complexity accounts?
What recurrent or self-modeling architecture is sufficient without over-attributing consciousness to ordinary adaptive systems?

records.name: Criticality hypothesis of consciousness
records.status: active empirical framework · heterogeneous evidence · contested
records.status_note: A 2023 scoping review found altered states generally associated with departures from criticality, but methods were inhomogeneous and most studies could not establish the direction of departure.
records.summary: The hypothesis holds that healthy conscious brain dynamics operate near a critical regime that balances integration and differentiation and supports a large repertoire, susceptibility, and flexible information processing. Unconscious or altered states are expected to shift away from that regime, although subcritical and supercritical directions may differ by state and metric.
records.scope: Dynamical-regime account of global conscious state and altered-state transitions across sleep, anesthesia, disorders of consciousness, epilepsy, psychedelics, delirium, and meditation.
records.boundary_note: Do not collapse into the Entropic Brain Hypothesis, which was formulated around psychedelic-state entropy, or into IIT, which makes a constitutive integrated-information claim. Criticality is a dynamical-regime hypothesis; entropy, avalanche statistics, long-range temporal correlations, and complexity are non-equivalent operationalizations.

claim_scope.target: Global state capacity, flexibility, and altered-state dynamics.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Why any critical dynamics are phenomenal, which conscious contents occur, or that every conscious system must sit at a thermodynamic phase transition.

basis: A multimodal 2016 study found large-scale signatures of unconsciousness consistent with departure from critical dynamics.
A 2023 scoping review retained 49 primary studies spanning seven altered-state categories and found broad evidence of deviation from criticality.
limitations: Criticality estimators and null models vary substantially, and finite-size or filtering effects can mimic critical signatures.
The review found that most studies could not determine whether deviations were subcritical or supercritical.
Covariation with arousal, connectivity, spectral slope, and generic signal complexity limits theory specificity.
evidence_profile.independence: The evidence spans independent groups and states, but conceptual and measurement heterogeneity prevents a single pooled adjudication.

open_questions: Which definition and estimator of criticality is valid across recording scales and conscious states?
Are departures from criticality causes, consequences, or correlates of altered consciousness?
Can prospective interventions move a brain toward criticality and restore consciousness without merely increasing arousal?

records.name: Neural Hierarchy model of consciousness
records.status: integrative proposal · component evidence available · untested as a whole
records.status_note: The model is a single-author synthesis. Layer-5 dendritic and central-thalamic components have causal animal evidence, but the proposed graded-to-nonlinear hierarchy has not been tested as one integrated theory.
records.summary: The model attempts to reconcile graded recurrent processing with nonlinear global ignition by positing lower- and higher-order thresholds in a processing hierarchy. It links graded detection and local recurrent activity to lower-order awareness, and nonlinear identification or higher-order awareness to bursting and recurrent output involving thick-tufted layer-5 pyramidal neurons and higher-order thalamocortical interactions.
records.scope: Multiscale model of conscious perceptual thresholds intended to bridge cellular neurophysiology, recurrent processing, and global cortical ignition.
records.boundary_note: Keep distinct from GNWT, RPT, Dendritic Integration Theory, and Apical Amplification. Neural Hierarchy is specifically an integrative graded-to-nonlinear levels-of-processing model; overlap in layer-5 dendrites and thalamocortical recurrence is evidence of shared mechanism, not identity among theories.

claim_scope.target: Lower- and higher-order conscious perceptual thresholds and their relation to graded versus all-or-none neural signatures.
claim_scope.level: Cellular, laminar, thalamocortical, and large-scale cortical.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That P3b is a pure consciousness marker, that layer-5 bursting is sufficient for phenomenality, or that the hierarchy generalizes beyond the tested perceptual domains.

basis: A peer-reviewed defining model-and-review explicitly states the graded lower-order and nonlinear higher-order architecture.
Causal mouse work shows apical dendritic activity in layer-5 pyramidal neurons shifts perceptual detection thresholds.
Macaque work shows central-lateral thalamic stimulation can modulate arousal and layer-specific cortical activity under anesthesia.
limitations: The component experiments were not designed to test the full Neural Hierarchy model.
Animal detection and anesthesia paradigms do not directly establish the proposed human phenomenological partition.
Ignition and P3b can be affected by task, report, attention, and post-perceptual processing.
evidence_profile.independence: Component evidence comes from independent laboratories; theory-level prospective tests are still absent.

open_questions: Can one experiment dissociate the predicted graded lower-order threshold from the nonlinear higher-order threshold without report confounds?
Which layer-5 cell classes and thalamic nuclei are necessary for each proposed level?
Does the hierarchy explain state consciousness, nonvisual content, and nonhuman experience as well as visual access?

records.name: Perturbational Complexity Index framework
records.status: validated research and clinical-assessment framework · interpretation bounded
records.status_note: PCI has independent validation across report-capable states and has stratified unresponsive patients, but it is an index of the brain's capacity for complex causal responses rather than a standalone theory or direct readout of experience.
records.summary: PCI perturbs cortex with transcranial magnetic stimulation and compresses the spatiotemporal EEG response to quantify the joint presence of distributed interaction and differentiated activity. It was designed to estimate conscious level without requiring sensory processing, command following, or behavioral report, then validated in wakefulness, dreaming, sleep, anesthesia, and severe brain injury.
records.scope: Theory-motivated TMS–EEG measurement and patient-stratification framework for global conscious capacity across physiological, pharmacological, and pathological states.
records.boundary_note: PCI is not IIT itself and a high PCI is not direct proof of phenomenality or content. Keep it distinct from behavioral diagnostic categories, cognitive-motor dissociation, and spontaneous EEG complexity measures because it estimates causal response complexity after controlled perturbation.

claim_scope.target: Global capacity for consciousness when behavioral report is unavailable.
claim_scope.level: Whole-cortex perturbational response measured with TMS–EEG.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Specific conscious content, moment-to-moment experience, a unique constitutive theory, or an infallible individual diagnosis.

basis: The original study tested PCI in healthy wakefulness, dreaming, NREM sleep, multiple anesthetics, and patients emerging from coma.
A 2016 independently validated cutoff was applied to stratify a large cohort of unresponsive patients and identify heterogeneous residual complexity.
limitations: Acquisition requires specialized stimulation, EEG, artifact control, and analyzable cortical responses.
Lesion location, medication, protocol, and hardware can affect responses and cross-site thresholds.
PCI estimates capacity and can remain silent about content or brief fluctuations.
evidence_profile.independence: The validation paper shares members of the originating consortium; external multicenter replication and protocol harmonization remain important.

open_questions: How stable are individual thresholds across devices, preprocessing pipelines, medications, and lesion etiologies?
How should PCI be combined with active-task fMRI/EEG evidence of cognitive-motor dissociation?
Can bedside variants preserve validity while reducing time, cost, and stimulation constraints?

records.name: Cognitive Unbinding paradigm
records.status: active mechanistic paradigm · convergent but non-unique evidence
records.status_note: Neuroimaging and neurophysiology support impaired large-scale synthesis as a common proximal feature of anesthesia, but anesthetic agents, doses, networks, and behavioral endpoints remain heterogeneous.
records.summary: Cognitive unbinding identifies impaired synthesis among specialized cognitive operations as a proximal mechanism of unconsciousness. In general anesthesia, molecularly diverse drugs may converge by disrupting the effective and functional interactions needed to bind distributed processing into coherent cognition; the paradigm has also been proposed as relevant to sleep and disorders of consciousness.
records.scope: Systems-level mechanism for anesthetic-induced unconsciousness and a candidate cross-state account of impaired cognitive integration.
records.boundary_note: This is a named proximal-mechanism paradigm nested under, but not duplicated by, the base catalog's generic anesthesia state. Keep separate from Neural Inertia, which concerns transition hysteresis, and cortical bistability, which specifies OFF-period dynamics. Unbinding does not posit one common molecular anesthetic target.

claim_scope.target: Proximal systems mechanism of loss of consciousness under general anesthesia and possibly related states.
claim_scope.level: Large-scale cognitive and neural network interactions.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A universal molecular endpoint, which connection is necessary in every agent and state, or that behavioral unresponsiveness always indicates absent experience.

basis: The defining review evaluates explicit tenets and predictions against neuroimaging and neurophysiology across anesthetic drug classes.
A later peer-reviewed review examines whether disrupted connectedness is a common anesthetic endpoint and separates molecular diversity from network convergence.
limitations: Connectivity measures depend on directionality assumptions, preprocessing, dose, task, and agent.
Some anesthesia can preserve isolated experience, dreaming, or disconnected consciousness despite absent responsiveness.
Network disconnection is shared with several competing theories and is not uniquely diagnostic of cognitive unbinding.
evidence_profile.independence: Both core sources include Mashour; evidence reviewed within them comes from multiple independent laboratories.

open_questions: Which directed interactions are causally necessary for connected versus disconnected consciousness?
Do all major anesthetic classes converge on the same network failure after pharmacokinetic and dose differences are controlled?
Can restoring selected connectivity re-establish experience without restoring overt responsiveness?

records.status: strong animal evidence · qualified human evidence
records.status_note: Hysteresis beyond simple pharmacokinetics is robust in flies and mice, while controlled human results depend on anesthetic, endpoint, and method. The model concerns resistance to state transition, not a full theory of consciousness.
records.summary: Neural Inertia proposes an active, biologically conserved barrier that resists transitions between wakefulness and anesthetic-induced unresponsiveness. The induction and emergence paths are therefore not necessarily mirror images: at the same drug level, the observed state can depend on prior state, producing hysteresis that sleep-wake genes and circuits can widen or collapse.
records.scope: Dynamical model of induction-emergence asymmetry and state stability under anesthesia, with proposed links to sleep-wake regulation.
records.boundary_note: Keep distinct from Cognitive Unbinding, which concerns loss of network synthesis after anesthesia, and from pharmacokinetic hysteresis alone. The observed endpoint is commonly loss or return of responsiveness; that endpoint must not be silently equated with the absence or return of subjective experience.

claim_scope.target: Path dependence and resistance at transitions between wakeful and anesthetic states.
claim_scope.level: Behavioral state dynamics linked to sleep-wake genes, circuits, and anesthetic pharmacology.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A constitutive mechanism of phenomenality, universal hysteresis for every drug and endpoint, or a clean equivalence between unresponsiveness and unconsciousness.

basis: The defining study demonstrated hysteresis not fully explained by pharmacokinetics across multiple anesthetics in Drosophila and mice and manipulated it with sleep-wake mutations.
A controlled human study tested propofol and sevoflurane with several behavioral and EEG endpoints.
limitations: The human study did not find significant induction-recovery differences for propofol and found endpoint- and co-medication-dependent effects for sevoflurane.
Apparent hysteresis can reflect equilibration, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling, endpoint selection, or population averaging.
Behavioral state barriers do not directly report disconnected or covert experience.
evidence_profile.independence: Human testing by an independent group both supports the relevance of the construct and materially narrows its universality.

open_questions: Which operational definition separates neural inertia from pharmacokinetic and measurement hysteresis in humans?
Which arousal circuits actively stabilize each side of the transition barrier?
Does neural inertia apply to sleep, coma recovery, and disconnected consciousness rather than only anesthetic responsiveness?

records.name: Cortical bistability / OFF-period account of impaired consciousness
records.status: mechanistically supported across NREM sleep and UWS · scope unresolved
records.status_note: Intracranial and TMS–EEG evidence links activation-dependent OFF-periods to interrupted causal propagation and reduced complexity, but generalization to all unconscious states and causal rescue remain open.
records.summary: The account proposes that when cortical circuits become bistable, an input can trigger a slow wave followed by an OFF-period or neuronal down-state. Activity later resumes, but the deterministic influence of the initiating event has been lost, preventing stable long-range causal interactions and complex responses. The mechanism has been observed in NREM sleep and in unresponsive wakefulness syndrome despite residual cortical activity and reactivity.
records.scope: Local cellular-to-network mechanism proposed to explain impaired causal integration and global conscious capacity in NREM sleep and severe brain injury.
records.boundary_note: This record is a candidate mechanism, not another measure. PCI quantifies the resulting perturbational complexity; the OFF-period account explains one way complexity may collapse. It is also distinct from seizure-related Network Inhibition and from anesthetic Cognitive Unbinding, although their network consequences may overlap.

claim_scope.target: Failure of sustained causal interaction in specific physiological and pathological low-consciousness states.
claim_scope.level: Activation-dependent local OFF-periods propagating consequences to global response complexity.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That every unconscious state contains cortical OFF-periods, that OFF-period absence proves consciousness, or that the mechanism specifies conscious content.

basis: Intracranial stimulation in eight epilepsy patients compared wakefulness with NREM sleep and linked OFF-periods to loss of deterministic phase-locked propagation.
TMS–EEG in 16 unresponsive-wakefulness patients, 20 healthy awake participants, and eight sleeping participants linked sleep-like OFF-periods to reduced local causality and global complexity.
limitations: The sleep study involved a small clinical intracranial sample, and the injury study involved heterogeneous lesions.
OFF-periods may be one of several mechanisms that reduce effective connectivity and complexity.
Both studies are observational with respect to subjective experience; direct selective reversal has not established necessity or sufficiency.
evidence_profile.independence: The two studies overlap substantially in research consortium and methods, so replication by independent groups is desirable.

open_questions: Are OFF-periods present in anesthesia, coma, seizures, and other states after controlling for spectral slow activity?
Can selective suppression of pathological OFF-periods restore complex causal interactions and reliable signs of consciousness?
How local must bistability be before global consciousness is impaired?

records.name: Two-stage discrete perception model
aliases: Two-stage discrete model of conscious perception
records.status: active psychophysical model · domain-limited and contested
records.status_note: Long-lasting postdictive effects motivate the model, but the duration, discreteness, neural implementation, and generalization beyond selected perceptual paradigms remain unresolved.
records.summary: The model separates quasi-continuous, high-temporal-resolution unconscious processing from discrete conscious percepts. Features, including temporal features, can be analyzed and integrated over an extended period; once processing converges, a coherent feature set is rendered conscious together, allowing later events to shape the experienced interpretation of earlier stimuli without requiring a stream of continuously revised conscious snapshots.
records.scope: Temporal architecture of conscious perception, developed primarily from visual psychophysics, feature fusion, masking, TMS, and postdictive phenomena.
records.boundary_note: This is a temporal model of conscious percept formation, not a complete theory of the substrate or function of consciousness. It differs from simple oscillatory snapshot theories: the first stage remains quasi-continuous and unconscious, and the authors do not infer conscious sampling rate directly from periodic behavior or sensory resolution.

claim_scope.target: When and how perceptual information becomes consciously available after extended unconscious integration.
claim_scope.level: Psychophysical and computational temporal organization, with only partial neural localization.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A universal duration for percepts, discrete consciousness in every modality and cognitive domain, or a necessary neural oscillator.

basis: The 2016 framework integrates visual illusions, feature fusion, temporal labeling, and TMS evidence into a two-stage architecture.
The 2020 review surveys long-lasting postdictive effects and argues they favor continuous unconscious processing followed by discrete conscious percepts.
limitations: Much of the evidence comes from selected visual paradigms in which alternative buffering, recurrent, and decision-level explanations remain possible.
Behavior and report constrain the timing of access but do not directly reveal the duration of an unreported percept.
Cross-modal, ecological, and neural-causal tests are limited.
evidence_profile.independence: Both core sources come from overlapping proponents; independent adversarial tests against continuous models are needed.

open_questions: What neural event marks the proposed transition from continuous unconscious processing to a discrete conscious percept?
Does the architecture generalize to audition, interoception, action, thought, and ongoing self-experience?
Which postdictive results uniquely favor discreteness over continuous recurrent integration plus delayed report?

records.name: Partial Awareness Hypothesis
records.status: active and contested hypothesis
records.status_note: The proposal remains a live account of graded and level-specific access, but evidence depends on how representational level, report, and subjective visibility are operationalized.
records.summary: Conscious access can occur independently at different levels of a representational hierarchy. An observer may therefore access some features of a stimulus while lacking access to higher-level identity or a fully integrated object representation, yielding partial rather than wholly present or absent awareness.
records.boundary_note: This is a hypothesis about the grain and level of conscious access. It is not the same claim as phenomenal overflow, and it does not by itself specify a neural mechanism or a metaphysics of consciousness.
records.claim_scope: Human visual awareness under masking and related psychophysical manipulations; specifically, whether access is graded across independently accessible representational levels.
records.evidence_profile: Psychophysical visibility reports, objective discrimination, masking, and manipulations of task-relevant processing level.
open_questions: Which experimental signatures uniquely distinguish partial awareness from response noise or mixed all-or-none states?
How stable is level-specific awareness across stimulus classes, report formats, and no-report measures?
Does partial access generalize beyond visual perception?

records.name: Nelson–Narens Monitoring–Control Framework
records.status: foundational framework · actively used
records.status_note: The two-level architecture remains foundational in metacognition research, while particular monitoring cues and control policies are modeled differently across tasks.
records.summary: Cognition is organized into an object level and a meta level. Information flowing from the object level to the meta level supports monitoring, while control signals from the meta level modify object-level operations such as study, retrieval, reporting, or termination.
records.boundary_note: The framework was developed for metacognition and metamemory. It does not entail that every monitoring signal is phenomenally conscious, nor is it a general theory of phenomenal consciousness.
records.claim_scope: Monitoring and strategic control of first-order cognitive operations, especially learning, memory retrieval, confidence, and voluntary reporting.
records.evidence_profile: Judgments of learning, feeling-of-knowing reports, confidence, optional reporting, study-time allocation, retrieval termination, and accuracy–quantity tradeoffs.
open_questions: Which monitoring signals are consciously accessible and which remain implicit?
How should reciprocal monitoring and control be implemented computationally across cognitive domains?
When do reports reflect monitoring quality rather than control policy or response incentives?

records.name: Meta-d′ and Metacognitive-Efficiency Framework
records.status: widely used measurement framework · assumptions actively debated
records.status_note: Meta-d′ and meta-d′/d′ are standard tools for separating confidence sensitivity from first-order performance, but estimates depend on signal-detection assumptions, trial counts, rating structure, and model specification.
records.summary: Meta-d′ expresses how much first-order signal, in d′ units, would be required for an ideal observer to produce the observed confidence discrimination between correct and incorrect decisions. Dividing meta-d′ by d′ yields an estimate of metacognitive efficiency relative to task sensitivity.
records.boundary_note: This is an inferential and measurement framework, not a substantive theory that confidence constitutes consciousness. High or low meta-d′ alone does not establish the presence or absence of phenomenal awareness.
records.claim_scope: Quantification of metacognitive sensitivity and efficiency from confidence or other type-2 judgments while controlling for first-order task sensitivity and response bias.
records.evidence_profile: Confidence-rating distributions, type-1 and type-2 receiver-operating characteristics, hierarchical model fits, and cross-task or cross-population comparisons.
open_questions: How robust are efficiency estimates when equal-variance and stationarity assumptions fail?
Which latent processes—evidence loss, additional noise, criterion variability, or post-decisional evidence—produce a given meta-d′ deficit?
How should meta-d′ be adapted for continuous, multi-alternative, or nonverbal reports?

records.name: Bayesian Second-Order Self-Evaluation Framework
records.status: active computational framework
records.status_note: The framework provides a normative account of confidence and error monitoring, while the brain's approximations, evidence sources, and task-specific departures from optimality remain under investigation.
records.summary: Self-evaluation is modeled as Bayesian inference about the performance of a coupled but distinct first-order decision system. Confidence and error detection combine a separate evidence sample with information about one's own choice, allowing dissociations between decision accuracy and metacognitive judgment without treating confidence as a direct readout of the decision variable.
records.boundary_note: This decision self-evaluation framework is distinct from the cataloged Higher-Order State Space account: its target is confidence and error monitoring about decisions, not the higher-order inference proposed to generate awareness itself.
records.claim_scope: Human confidence, error detection, and metacognitive calibration in perceptual and value-based decisions.
records.evidence_profile: Bayesian ideal-observer modeling, confidence distributions, error reports, performance–confidence dissociations, and comparison of fitted latent evidence variables.
open_questions: What neural computations approximate the proposed second-order inference?
When does confidence use the same evidence as choice versus post-decisional or action-related evidence?
How does the framework generalize to memory, learning, and social self-evaluation?

records.name: Self-Memory System
records.tradition: Autobiographical memory / cognitive psychology of self
records.status: influential active framework
records.status_note: The Self-Memory System continues to organize research on autobiographical remembering, identity, and goal regulation; its component structure and neural implementation are still refined.
records.summary: Autobiographical memories are transient constructions produced by interaction between an autobiographical knowledge base and a working self composed of current goals and self-images. The knowledge base constrains who one has been and can be, while the working self regulates access to memory in the service of coherence and adaptive correspondence.
records.boundary_note: The framework explains autobiographical memory and diachronic self-representation. It does not reduce all selfhood to narrative memory and does not claim that memory construction alone explains phenomenal consciousness.
records.claim_scope: Construction, retrieval, organization, and self-regulation of autobiographical memories and their contribution to temporally extended identity.
records.evidence_profile: Autobiographical recall, memory specificity, goal effects, clinical and neuropsychological dissociations, lifespan development, and neuroimaging of autobiographical remembering.
open_questions: How are working-self goals implemented and updated neurally?
How does the system balance accurate correspondence with self-coherence under conflict?
Which parts of autobiographical construction require autonoetic consciousness?

records.name: Neisser's Multiple-Selves Framework
records.status: foundational taxonomy · continuing influence
records.status_note: The taxonomy remains influential in developmental and embodied-self research, though the proposed informational separability and direct-perception claims are not a settled consensus.
records.summary: Self-knowledge arises from multiple informational sources rather than a single self-representation. Neisser distinguishes ecological, interpersonal, extended, private, and conceptual selves; the ecological and interpersonal selves are proposed to emerge early through information specifying one's relation to the physical and social environment.
records.boundary_note: The ecological and interpersonal self are perceptual organizations of self-related information, not equivalent to explicit self-concept, narrative identity, mirror recognition, or reflective phenomenal self-consciousness.
records.claim_scope: Sources and developmental trajectories of self-knowledge, especially directly perceived bodily–environmental and interpersonal relations.
records.evidence_profile: Ecological perception, visual–proprioceptive contingency, infant social interaction, developmental observation, and conceptual analysis of distinct self-information sources.
open_questions: To what degree are ecological and interpersonal self-information directly specified rather than inferentially represented?
How do the five proposed selves interact across development?
Which components are necessary for explicit or phenomenal self-awareness?

records.name: Joint Attention
records.status: core active developmental construct
records.status_note: Joint attention is a mature research domain, but definitions and measures distinguish gaze following, responding to joint attention, initiating joint attention, and sustained joint engagement.
records.summary: Joint attention is the coordination of two individuals' attention with respect to an object or event, including behavior that follows, directs, or sustains another's attention and, in stronger formulations, represents the focus as shared. It is a major developmental context for communication and social learning.
records.boundary_note: Gaze following alone need not demonstrate awareness that attention is mutually shared. Joint attention is related to, but not identical with, full belief attribution, shared intentionality, or phenomenal consciousness.
records.claim_scope: Development and function of coordinated attention in infant–caregiver interaction, communication, reference, learning, and later social cognition.
records.evidence_profile: Gaze and point following, alternating gaze, declarative and imperative gestures, joint engagement, longitudinal language outcomes, and developmental or clinical comparison.
open_questions: Which behavioral criteria distinguish shared-attention representation from directional cue following?
How do initiating and responding to joint attention rely on different mechanisms?
Which aspects are shared with nonhuman animals and which depend on human communicative norms?

records.name: False-Belief Understanding
records.status: foundational paradigm · interpretation actively contested
records.status_note: Explicit false-belief tasks remain central operational measures, but performance is influenced by language, executive demand, task format, and population-specific factors; task failure is not a sufficient diagnosis of absent theory of mind.
records.summary: False-belief understanding is the capacity to represent that another agent's belief can differ from reality and from one's own knowledge, and to use that attributed belief when predicting or explaining the agent's action. Classic unexpected-transfer tasks operationalize explicit belief attribution.
records.boundary_note: This record catalogs a target construct and experimental family, not a unitary theory of mind. A correct response does not exhaust theory-of-mind competence, and an incorrect response does not by itself establish mindblindness or lack of social understanding.
records.claim_scope: Explicit tracking and action prediction based on another person's mistaken belief, principally in developmental and clinical experimental tasks.
records.evidence_profile: Unexpected-transfer and unexpected-contents tasks, verbal prediction and explanation, anticipatory behavior, developmental trajectories, task-manipulation studies, and clinical comparisons.
open_questions: How much performance variance reflects belief representation versus language and executive control?
Do implicit and explicit false-belief paradigms measure the same capacity?
How should tasks be adapted without treating neurodivergent social cognition as a global deficit?

records.name: Teleological Stance and Naïve Theory of Rational Action
records.status: influential developmental account · actively debated
records.status_note: Evidence supports early sensitivity to goal efficiency and situational constraints, while debate continues over whether those findings require teleological representation, mental-state attribution, lower-level perceptual mechanisms, or learned expectations.
records.summary: Young infants interpret actions by relating an observed movement, a goal state, and situational constraints through a principle of rational action: agents are expected to select an efficient available means to their goal. The early teleological stance is proposed as nonmentalistic and developmentally prior to a later stance that represents beliefs and desires.
records.boundary_note: The teleological stance explicitly analyzes action without initially attributing propositional mental states. It is therefore distinct from Dennett's intentional stance, full belief–desire mindreading, and the cataloged Theory-Theory family.
records.claim_scope: Infant and adult interpretation of goal-directed action under constraints, especially expectations of rational efficiency.
records.evidence_profile: Habituation and violation-of-expectation paradigms, goal-change and constraint manipulations, referential action studies, and developmental comparison.
open_questions: What evidence distinguishes principle-based teleological reasoning from perceptual novelty or learned action regularities?
When and how does nonmentalistic teleology develop into explicit belief–desire attribution?
How domain-specific is the rational-action principle?

records.name: Bayesian Theory of Mind and Inverse Planning
records.status: active computational research program
records.status_note: The framework quantitatively predicts judgments in controlled action-understanding tasks, while its approximate-rationality assumptions and generalization to natural social behavior remain active research issues.
records.summary: Observers are modeled as inverting a generative model in which an agent plans approximately rationally given its beliefs, desires, percepts, and environment. Bayesian inference combines observed actions with priors to recover probability distributions over those latent mental states.
records.boundary_note: This is a specific probabilistic formalization of mental-state inference. It is not merely an alias for Theory-Theory, Dennett's intentional stance, or the teleological stance, and model success does not establish that people explicitly compute the fitted Bayesian quantities.
records.claim_scope: Quantitative attribution of goals, beliefs, desires, and percepts from observed action under a generative model of approximately rational planning.
records.evidence_profile: Behavioral probability judgments, animated-maze and choice tasks, generative model comparison, inverse planning, and quantitative prediction of belief–desire attribution.
open_questions: How are priors and subjective models of other agents learned?
How does inference handle irrationality, habit, emotion, communication, and norm-following?
Which computational approximations can scale to continuous, multi-agent social environments?

records.name: Mindshaping Account of Social Cognition
records.tradition: Philosophy of cognitive science / cultural evolution
records.status: active minority framework
records.status_note: Mindshaping is a developed alternative emphasis within social-cognition theory, but the claimed explanatory priority of regulative practices over sophisticated mindreading remains contested.
records.summary: Human social cognition relies not only on reading already formed minds but on practices that shape dispositions, expectations, narratives, and norms so that behavior becomes easier to coordinate and interpret. On the stronger account, sophisticated propositional-attitude attribution depends developmentally and evolutionarily on prior mindshaping practices.
records.boundary_note: Mindshaping is not an alias for mindreading, interaction theory, social conformity, or collective intentionality. Its distinctive claim concerns the explanatory and evolutionary role of practices that make minds behaviorally interpretable.
records.claim_scope: Developmental, cultural, and evolutionary functions of imitation, pedagogy, norm enforcement, expectation, and narrative in stabilizing socially interpretable cognition and behavior.
records.evidence_profile: Philosophical argument drawing on developmental psychology, social psychology, cultural evolution, niche construction, pedagogy, imitation, norm conformity, and narrative self-constitution.
open_questions: How should mindshaping be operationalized independently of mindreading and ordinary social influence?
Which regulative practices are necessary for propositional-attitude attribution?
What comparative and developmental evidence would distinguish causal priority from reciprocal co-development?

records.name: Natural Pedagogy
records.status: influential active account · debated
records.status_note: Sensitivity to ostensive communication is well studied, while the strength of kind-generalization biases, cultural universality, human specificity, and status as an evolved adaptation remain debated.
records.summary: Human communication is proposed to include a specialized system for transmitting generic, cognitively opaque cultural knowledge. Infants are receptive to ostensive signals that mark communication, expect a referential target, and tend to interpret ostensive demonstrations as conveying kind-relevant and generalizable information.
records.boundary_note: Natural pedagogy is a theory of communicative social learning, not a general theory of consciousness. It is distinct from all teaching behavior, imitation alone, shared intentionality, and the broader claim that learning is social.
records.claim_scope: Infant and human receptivity to ostensive–referential communication and the transmission of generic cultural knowledge.
records.evidence_profile: Eye contact and infant-directed communication, gaze and reference, imitation of causally opaque actions, object-function learning, generalization tests, and cross-cultural or comparative studies.
open_questions: When do ostensive cues promote generic learning versus episodic or person-specific learning?
How culturally variable are the cues and resulting inductive biases?
Does evidence support a human-specific evolved adaptation rather than interacting general mechanisms?

records.name: Mirror Self-Recognition and the Mark Test
records.status: widely used paradigm · construct interpretation contested
records.status_note: The mark test is a historically important operational assay of visual self-recognition. Species conclusions and inferences from task success or failure remain sensitive to sensory ecology, motivation, experience, and the definition of self-awareness.
records.summary: After experience with a mirror, an individual may use the reflected image to inspect or touch a covert mark that cannot otherwise be seen. Such mark-directed behavior is treated as evidence that the subject relates the image to its own body rather than treating it only as another individual.
records.boundary_note: Mirror self-recognition is an operational indicator of visual self-recognition, not a sufficient test of phenomenal consciousness, a unitary self-concept, or general self-awareness. Failure cannot rule out nonvisual forms of self-knowledge.
records.claim_scope: Visual recognition of one's reflected body in human development and comparative animal cognition.
records.evidence_profile: Mirror exposure, contingency testing, covert-mark behavior, developmental sequences, species comparison, modified sensory paradigms, and replication or critique of mark-directed responses.
open_questions: What cognitive representation is minimally required for mark-directed behavior?
How should the paradigm be adapted for species whose primary sensory ecology is not visual?
Which aspects of self-recognition generalize beyond mirrors and body appearance?

records.name: Comparative Animal Metacognition and Uncertainty Monitoring
records.status: active and methodologically contested research program
records.status_note: Multiple species show adaptive uncertainty or information-seeking behavior, but whether particular results require metacognitive monitoring rather than associative, behavioral-cue, or response-competition accounts is evaluated paradigm by paradigm.
records.summary: Comparative metacognition research tests whether nonhuman animals monitor the strength or availability of their own perceptual and memory information. Subjects may decline difficult trials, seek information, or selectively take memory tests; transfer and cue-control procedures aim to distinguish internal monitoring from learned external associations.
records.boundary_note: Adaptive uncertainty responses do not automatically establish explicit metarepresentation, human-like self-reflection, or phenomenal consciousness. The record concerns a research framework and target capacity, not a single mechanism shared across species.
records.claim_scope: Behavioral monitoring of uncertainty, perceptual difficulty, memory availability, and information need in nonhuman animals.
records.evidence_profile: Uncertainty-response and opt-out tasks, prospective and retrospective wagering, information seeking, optional memory tests, transfer tests, cue controls, species comparison, and associative-model challenges.
open_questions: Which paradigms exclude public-cue and reinforcement-history explanations most convincingly?
Do uncertainty monitoring and metamemory share a domain-general process within individual animals?
What level of self-representation, if any, is required for successful performance?
